verdict.label: duplicate
verdict.why: Both functions repeat the same realtime provider-transform round trip. Each packs the seven session-state fields (output item id, response id, conversation id, delta chunks, item chunks, delta type, session_configuration_request) into `realtime_response_transform_input`. Each then calls `transform_realtime_response(message, model, logging_obj, ...)`, writes the same seven returned fields back into its session state, and normalizes `response` from a single item or a list into a list of events. A shared helper such as `transform_realtime_message(config, message, model, logging_obj, state) -> list[event]` would own that state marshaling and the list normalization. The state container is the only legitimate variation, since NEW keeps it as attributes on `self` and EXISTING keeps it in a `session_state` dict. A small adapter or a state dict would cover that. Everything after the transform stays in the callers. That includes NEW's guardrail, session.created and VAD handling, and EXISTING's send-to-client, end-of-stream and logging-filter handling. The overlap is only the transform-and-state-sync step, not the whole functions.
